4.en: ‘I carry with me an Inquisitorial Seal. It is a small, unassuming object contained in a neat box. It is a modest thing. Relatively plain, adorned with a single motif and a simple motto. Yet with this little object, I can sign the death warrant of an entire world and consign a billion souls to oblivion.’

22.en: Despite the average citizen’s belief that the Inquisition is effectively omnipotent, its Inquisitors cannot be everywhere at once — many crimes and injustices fall below what is worth their time and resources to investigate, and the same goes for their acolytes. Members of the Inquisition must consider their prime targets above all else, be it the daemon, heretic, or xenos. Sometimes, Inquisitors of the Ordo Malleus may be called upon to deal with a xenos threat. But, lesser infringements of any other kind are under the remit of the Imperium’s other factions and organisations and should be remedied by them.

26.en: It is rare that an investigation is ever a simple affair. Inquisitors and acolytes alike can dedicate years or decades of their lives towards pursuing a single threat or goal, with many of those years operating in total secrecy (see Long-Term Endeavours). Many investigations start subtly, with Inquisitor@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.r6clx5uYnIpkdaRq.JournalEntryPage.56xpJ7ADckt2kxHB]{Inquisition Long-Term Endeavours}s aiming to thwart a threat before civilian awareness occurs. Inquisitors see their acolytes as small, precise, and expendable tools that can work in the shadows while overseeing their operations in a more public-facing form. Ultimate authority may be just that, but most Inquisitors know it works best when applied in the right place at the right time. Some investigations can pass a point of no return, where the Inquisitor is forced to rally troops and effectively march to war, with a greater potential for collateral damage and exposure.

42.en: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.KbejcPMug5gfoWWz]{Subtlety} encompasses a new ruleset to enhance Inquisition-focused campaigns. It grants rewards and sanctions for operating at different levels of covert behaviour. GMs and their Players should discuss implementing these rules before beginning or adding them to their campaign, ensuring that everyone understands the causality and benefits of their actions.

70.en: The Inquisition’s infamous last resort. To unleash the ultimate sanction of Exterminatus upon a world is to consider it lost to damnation — an unavoidable scouring of all life upon a planet so that it is completely purged of corruption, often via excessive orbital bombardment or superweapon. Many citizens have heard legends, myths, or rumours of worlds that have been wiped off the star charts by inquisitorial order, but few know for sure. The Inquisition ensures that public knowledge of such events is expunged.

78.en: This declaration signifies an individual having cavorted with or been knowingly influenced by daemons. It often applies to rogue psykers or those practising forbidden arts; even some Inquisitors of the Ordo Malleus have been declared Extremis Diabolus after degenerating into Radical behaviour. It is similar to Excommunicate Traitoris but further acts as an extreme warning to stay away from such corrupted individuals.

86.en: This declaration is branded upon those, typically large groups, who refuse to comply with the Imperium’s laws and are often beyond the reach of Imperial authority. During the Macharian Crusade, many lost worlds were given an ultimatum to rejoin the Imperium or forever become its enemy — those who rebuffed the offer received this designation, forever to be treated no better than xenos.

98.en: It is rare for an Inquisitor to bestow their @UUID[.8VTOoxqcL2uC3eZm#the-inquisitorial-rosette]{Rosette} to any acolyte under them — but because they cannot be everywhere at once, some opt to provide their agents with sanctioned simulacra of their original. These copies may be further gene-locked to prevent misuse in the wrong hands or even have a timed window of use built-in before they become inert or self-destruct. Acolytes should be careful when bearing the Rosette publicly, as it may raise the stakes of their investigation in unforeseen ways or announce the Inquisition’s presence in places better served undiscovered.
